extracted.intended_audience: government communicators (GCS members / UK civil servants responsible for public communications)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and guidance for professional government communicators in the UK covering required competencies, campaign planning, quality assurance, propriety, accessibility, channel-specific guidance and mandatory evaluation and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards for government communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the Government Communication Service (GCS) is to provide an exceptional standard of professional practice in support of the government, implementing priorities of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet to build a stronger economy, a fairer society, a United Kingdom and a global Britain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCS maintains a suite of professional standards guidance to support and quality assure work, to make the best standard, and to build a world-class public communications profession. GCS members commit to observing the highest standard of communications practice, professional development and ethics. The professional standards include mandatory evaluation of communications activity, and completion of over 4 pieces of professional development during the year, as part of the evaluation framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Functional Standard for Communication (GovS011)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HM Government Functional Standard for Communication (‘GovS011’), also called Communication Government Functional Standard, gives a comprehensive baseline for the communications profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GovS011 brings together GCS initiatives ranging from MCOM2.0 to the Professional Assurance (PASS) process for spending and the competency framework; it serves as the baseline standard for roles, responsibilities and expected practice in government communications (updated September 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Framework (QAF)
rubrics_metrics.description: A framework that brings together standards on a single page to show how they work in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The QAF validates and promotes 'next level' excellence in public service communication and shows how governance, assurance and quality processes apply in practice to communication activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern Communications Operating Model (MCOM2.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model setting out the essential skills, capabilities and practices required for an effective public service communications profession and function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCOM2.0 defines the disciplines, capabilities and operating practices expected of teams delivering government communications, and is referenced as a core component of professional baseline and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide to campaign planning: OASIS
rubrics_metrics.description: OASIS: Objective, Audience insight, Strategy, Implementation, Scoring/evaluation — a guide to campaign planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of this guide is to ensure that all government communications are effective, efficient and evaluated. It helps develop campaign plans and structure thinking by requiring clear objectives, audience insight, strategic approach, implementation plans and scoring/evaluation of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive guide on best practice in propriety, made specifically for government communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides standards and examples of correct/proper conduct in government communications to ensure appropriateness, impartiality and adherence to legal or ministerial rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication practices (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: GCS guidance covering MCOM disciplines and specific skills under the heading 'communication practices'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an umbrella for detailed practice-level guidance across disciplines (see specific practice entries such as crisis communication, accessibility, social media, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included under communication practices; intended to set expectations and practices for timely, accurate and coordinated messaging during emergencies and high-risk incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Planning Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A framework for planning communications during emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides structure and standards for pre-planned and responsive communications to support emergency response and public safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESIST 3: Building resilience to information threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance focused on building resilience to information threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out practices to identify, resist and counter deliberate misinformation or hostile information activity as part of safeguarding public communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devolution: Guidance for civil servants
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on communications practice where devolution to constituent nations applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises civil servants on nuances and requirements when communicating in devolved contexts (e.g., differences in responsibilities, coordination with devolved administrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to make communications accessible and inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Accessible communications', 'Five principles to make your campaigns more inclusive', and 'Communicating bilingually (on GOV.UK)' — practical standards to ensure campaigns are inclusive (accessibility, language, and audience needs), including specific guidance when communicating in Wales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style guide (spelling and grammar conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritative style guidance for spelling and grammar conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt consistent spelling and grammar conventions across communications; linked GOV.UK style guide provides specific rules and examples for clarity and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding guidelines for HM Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and standards for government branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets standards for visual identity and brand application across government communications to maintain a consistent and authoritative appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media playbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using social media for government communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides platform-specific best practice, channel strategy, and behavioural guidance for engaging audiences on social platforms (hosted on GOV.UK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning and development requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and requirements for professional development: GCS Academy, Competency Framework, Leadership Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCS members are expected to complete professional development (over four pieces per year as part of evaluation); these resources define competencies, training pathways and leadership development to meet the professional standards.
